scope: DoRobot Studio user journeys: robot setup, operate, record, save and replay. Desktop UI review and executable integration checks; physical robot calibration is not certified by this score.
evaluator: Model-authored review with instrumented real-input evidence; not an independent human usability study.
hard_gates: A new user can start a supported simulation without a terminal or socket path.
Simulation recording produces a real playable dataset with all three cameras and measured joints.
Real robot and simulation setup explain different calibration requirements.
Unsupported Nano arm calibration and camera acquisition are never presented as available.
Navigation preserves live operation, recording, pending takes and flexible panel layouts.
Errors, missing devices and incomplete calibration give an actionable recovery path.
No essential control is clipped at 1024x768 or 1440x900 in light or dark appearance.

dimensions.criteria: One clear setup-to-replay sequence; current source, current page and next action are unambiguous; advanced tools do not compete with the primary task.
Real and simulated setup are distinct; capabilities, prerequisites, calibration prompts, completion and blocking conditions are accurate and actionable.
Start, readiness, controls, reset, stop and reconnection work in the app; the user can identify the robot and environment.
Choose task and destination, record, stop, review, save/discard and open replay form one complete journey; actual captured data matches the UI's claims.
Navigation and appearance preserve work; busy/disabled states explain why; failures retain data and offer recovery.
Readable text, compact headers, consistent centered controls, visible state and unclipped responsive layout; preserve user-preferred panel behavior.

anchors.0.8: Usable with evident friction or an untested required UI state
anchors.0.95: Clear, complete and verified with only minor friction
anchors.1: All stated criteria verified without a material UX defect

scoring: Freeze this rubric before changes. Cite evidence and outstanding limitations per dimension. A failed hard gate prevents a passing verdict regardless of numeric score. Missing real hardware must be disclosed separately; never substitute mock calibration for physical verification.
